sections.h2: Where a Wayne County deed gets filed
sections.html:
The Recorder sits behind the first-floor doors of the Administration Building, 428 West Liberty Street, Wooster, OH 44691. The phone is 330-287-5460. This office keeps the legal documents of the county, chiefly real estate papers such as deeds, mortgages and liens. Subdivision plats are filed there too.

The Auditor, Treasurer, Board of Revision and Map Office occupy the same building, so most of a sale's paperwork can be done in one place.

The route is posted on the Auditor's real estate page, and a deed that skips a stop tends to come back unrecorded.

  • Draft the deed, then present it at the Map Office.
  • Carry it to the Auditor, where the conveyance and transfer charges are paid.
  • Last, file at the Recorder's counter.

The state's value statement sits behind the Auditor's stop. R.C. 319.202 requires a declaration of value from the grantee before endorsement. An exempt transfer states its reason in place of a value, using the exemption form DTE 100(EX) from the Auditor's library.

The Auditor charges $4.00 per thousand dollars of price and $0.50 per parcel, applied after the price is bumped up to the next $100. The Tools menu on the Auditor's site includes a Conveyance Fee Calculator for the arithmetic. The grantor owes the conveyance charge.

Unpaid taxes can stall a closing. Phone the Treasurer at 330-287-5450 for a payoff, and look at the delinquent list online. The Auditor, 330-287-5430, answers conveyance questions from 8:00 am on weekdays.

The table follows R.C. 317.32, in which each of the base and housing trust fund shares is $17 for pages one and two and $4 for every page after. A county may also add a preservation surcharge capped at $5, so ask the Recorder whether the total includes one.

The $20.00 line is aimed at papers that break the layout rules of R.C. 317.114, so check margins and ink with the Recorder before you sign.

sections.h2: What to bring to the counter
sections.html:
Take the endorsed original, parcel numbers and a check. Some name changes require a new deed, so compare the owner's name on the Auditor's parcel record with the deed before you file.

  • Land records at the Recorder are indexed by document type and parties.
  • A mortgage release is its own recording, with a marginal reference charge under the statute.
  • The Auditor's parcel search and GIS parcel viewer show earlier owners, acreage and last sale before the deed is written.

sections.h2: The value statement on a sale
sections.html:
The statute counts the full price paid or owed, mortgage and vendor's lien amounts included. A gift is valued at its likely open market price. Willfully misstating value is prohibited.

Two more questions ride along. One covers owner-occupied credit and homestead reductions. The other covers agricultural use valuation and any recoupment charge. A yes to either means both parties confirm the amount has been accounted for.

sections.h2: Tax due dates and your closing
sections.html:
Installment bills are issued in January or February and again in June or July. The last days at the Treasurer fall in late February and late July. A 10 percent penalty follows, and half is returned if the balance clears within 10 days.

If a deed records in the same week a bill comes due, put in writing who pays. Bank payments face earlier cutoffs than payments at the Treasurer. Partial payments are accepted and all go toward the upcoming bill.

sections.h2: Four phone numbers a seller needs
sections.html:
• Recorder, 330-287-5460.
  • Auditor, 330-287-5430.
  • Treasurer, 330-287-5450.
  • Board of Revision, 330-287-5433.

Call ahead with your parcel number in hand. The first handles recording, the second conveyance and parcel records, the third balances and payments, and the fourth valuation complaints. All answer from the same Wooster address.

sections.h2: Can a new owner file a value complaint after a sale?
sections.html:
Usually, yes. R.C. 5715.19 generally bars a second complaint on one parcel inside an interim period. Exceptions follow an arm's length sale, a casualty loss, a substantial improvement or a 15 percent occupancy change after the earlier lien date. A sale can therefore reopen the door for a parcel the seller already contested.

Filing opens each January 1, and for tax year 2026 the Auditor lists January 1 to March 31, 2027. Signatures must be notarized, which Auditor staff can usually do in person. The second half bill is held until the Board rules, and the first half stays payable on time.

sections.h2: Taxes after the deed is recorded
sections.html: Assessed value is 35 percent of market value, multiplied by the district rate and trimmed by a reduction factor. The owner-occupied credit has its own application, form DTE 105C, in the Auditor's library. Rates differ by district, and the Treasurer's website charts them all.

sections.h2: Online tools to use before recording
sections.html:
• Auditor: a parcel search and map, a conveyance calculator, a tax estimator, a levy estimator, sales reports and a delinquency report, plus downloadable forms.
  • Treasurer: payment through Autoagent online or at 1-844-615-1900, and monthly or semi-annual ACH direct debit for parcels that owe current taxes.
  • Recorder: a call to 330-287-5460 settles questions about what a particular paper needs.

Run the sales report and tax estimator first. They show what nearby parcels sold for and what the levies on your district would produce, which helps when you write the value into the statement.

Owners hold 76.6 percent of Wayne County homes, and the middle owner-held home is worth $222,100. About 59,000 parcels exist in the county, so most recorded deeds touch only a small slice of them in any year. If you are selling for cash, the same four steps apply: Map Office, Auditor, Recorder, and a tax payoff from the Treasurer.

Plan your trip in this order. First, confirm with the Treasurer that nothing is owed on the parcel. Second, have the deed drafted and take it to the Map Office. Third, pay the Auditor and collect the endorsement. Fourth, walk the deed down to the Recorder with a check for the right amount. If your lender is releasing an old mortgage, ask the title company to confirm the release is filed as its own recording. Keep a copy of the recorded deed and the receipt, since your buyer's lender and your own tax records may both ask for them later. A cash buyer will want the same proof of recording, so bring a second copy of the receipt to the closing table and give it to the closing agent at that time.

faqs.q: Where in Wooster do I file a Wayne County deed?
faqs.a: With the Recorder, 330-287-5460, in the Administration Building. Get the Auditor's endorsement first.

faqs.q: What recording fees apply in Wayne County?
faqs.a: The list is $34.00 for two pages, $8.00 per added page, $4.00 per marginal notation, $2.00 per copy and a $20.00 standardization fee. A preservation surcharge of up to $5 is optional under state law.

faqs.q: What does the Auditor take at the Wayne County conveyance step?
faqs.a: The Auditor charges $4.00 per $1,000 of price and $0.50 per parcel. The grantor owes the conveyance charge.

faqs.q: Is the Auditor's stop before or after the Recorder in Wayne County?
faqs.a: Before. The sequence is Map Office, Auditor, then Recorder.

faqs.q: Who gives a tax payoff on a Wayne County parcel?
faqs.a: The Treasurer, at 330-287-5450. Its website also shows a delinquent list.
